name: Sound_Command_ExecuteList
summary: Runs one round of the sound thread's queued-command list: walks command->next (first word) and switches on the one-byte opcode at +4, applying opcodes 2..0x3A to the target object held at +0x10, then moves to the next node. Opcodes 0x0D/0x0E/0x0F/0x22/0x23 land on the per-player parameter setters in this batch and 0x30..0x3A on the 12 channel/voice broadcast helpers, so this is the consumer side of the sound command queue.
evidence: 48 callees, every one inside 0x0054Exxx-0x00556xxx; opcode 0x3A calls 0x00550B78/0x00550D48, the queue helpers that Sound_SetOutputMode (N_007, 0x0054F604) uses when it enqueues a 0x3A node; opcode 0x0E forwards two vectors to 0x00554BC4, exactly the 3+13 word layout that 0x00548F90 builds; opcode 0x0D forwards to 0x005551F8 and 0x0F to 0x005556A0. No direct caller in the image, i.e. it is invoked from the sound thread loop by pointer.

name: maybe_Sound_Command_SubmitVectorPair
signature: void maybe_Sound_Command_SubmitVectorPair(SoundPlayer* owner, u32* vectors, u32* origin)
summary: Builds and enqueues sound command 0x0E aimed at the sub-object at owner+0x128: copies a 3-word vector from origin, then 8 further words and five 2-word pairs from vectors (13 words) into the command payload before submitting it on the current thread's command queue.
evidence: Writes payload offsets +0x14..+0x50 (3 + 13 words); the 0x0E handler 0x00554BC4 stores exactly 3 then 13 words into the sequence player's 0x168..0x1AC block; node allocation/submit via 0x0011B57C / 0x0011B89C, the same pair the sound voice pool and the fs request path use; target is always owner+0x128.

name: maybe_Sound_Command_SubmitValuesAndTimer
signature: void maybe_Sound_Command_SubmitValuesAndTimer(SoundPlayer* owner, u32 a, u32 b, u32 c, u8 d, u8 e, u64 timer)
summary: Builds and enqueues sound command 0x0D for owner+0x128 with three u32 values, two bytes and a 64-bit timer, then submits it. The 0x0D handler 0x005551F8 reads the same three-word payload and the two trailing counts.
evidence: Payload +0x14..+0x28 = arg2,arg3,arg4,arg5,arg6,arg7(lo,hi); opcode byte at +4 = 0x0D; handler 0x005551F8 (batch 0x005551F8 is not in this batch but is called from the same dispatcher case) consumes a mask plus two values from +0x14.

name: maybe_Sound_Command_SubmitTenWords
signature: void maybe_Sound_Command_SubmitTenWords(SoundPlayer* owner, u32* values, u32* extra)
summary: Builds and enqueues sound command 0x0F for owner+0x128 with ten u32 arguments; when extra[2] > 0 it also enqueues a second command (0x10) carrying a byte and a count, then sets owner+0x121 ('initialised').
evidence: Payload +0x14..+0x38 = values[0..9]; opcode byte 0x0F; handler 0x005556A0 reads the same ten-word block; second node is opcode 0x10 with (u8, count) which matches dispatcher case 0x10 -> 0x00555174(arg1[4], arg1[5]&0xff, arg1[6]); owner+0x121 is also the flag cleared by 0x00549288/0x00556E68.

name: maybe_Sound_Stream_Request_Cancel
summary: Cancels an in-flight sound-stream request: if the request is marked active (+0x120) it clears that flag and the +0x121 sub-flag, releases the sub-object, then under the owner context's critical section calls vtable+0x10 (abort) and releases the wait pair at owner+0x14/+0x18.
evidence: byte-identical twin at 0x00556E68; 0x00546EA0 (maybe_Sound_Voice_Release, N_034) on the sub-object, 0x0011FCBC/0x0011FCF8 on the owner context's +0x14/+0x18 wait pair; the +0x120/+0x121 flags are set by the loaders 0x00549FFC/0x00549154 and read by 0x005498FC.

name: Sound_Cwav_Open
signature: SoundCwavInfo* Sound_Cwav_Open(SoundCwavInfo* info, u32* cwav, int requireData)
summary: Validates a 3DS CWAV wave file and resolves its INFO and DATA sub-blocks. Requires the 'CWAV' magic (and, when requireData is 0, a plausible version/size), then finds the 'INFO' and 'DATA' chunk tags through 0x00663308/0x006632A0 and stores the wave pointer plus both chunk pointers.
evidence: g_005494f0 = 0x56415743 ('CWAV'), g_005494f4 = 0x4F464E49 ('INFO'), g_005494f8 = 0x41544144 ('DATA'); 0x00663308/0x006632A0 are the chunk finders; the result struct is consumed by 0x0065EF6C/0x006605B4 (INFO field readers) and 0x0054FE18 (start a wave); CWAV is the standard 3DS wave container and everything else in this batch is a DSP channel mixer.

name: maybe_Svc_SetFieldLocked
summary: Stores value into object->f_180 while holding the monitor at object->f_184. A three-line setter used wherever a shared sound state word must be published atomically.
evidence: 0x00117E50/0x00117ED0 are the monitor lock/unlock pair seen in dozens of other functions here (they appear as Os_LockMonitor in N_027 outputs); +0x180/+0x184 is the guarded field pair.

name: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecoded
signature: int maybe_Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecoded(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, u32 size, SoundAllocator* alloc, u32 flags)
summary: Decodes one CWAV wave into memory: asks the cache whether the id is already present, looks the entry up (0x0065E340) or resolves it (0x0054A230), allocates size+0x20 through the allocator vtable, writes the 0x20-byte in-memory wave header ('CIWV', id, size) and decodes the payload with 0x0054B12C. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: g_0054a16c = 0x56574943 ('CIWV' in-memory header tag), 0x20-byte memcpy via 0x00116A14; allocator calls (**(code**)(*arg4+8))(arg4,size) and bounds check against 0x001180E0/0x001180F0 (heap range); decode call 0x0054B12C; entry lookup 0x0065E340; called by 0x0054A170, 0x0054A8D0, 0x0054ABB0.

name: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_Preload
signature: int maybe_Sound_WaveCache_Preload(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, u32 size, SoundAllocator* alloc, u32 flags, u32 extra)
summary: Preloads one wave id into the cache: if the entry is already resident it returns 1, otherwise it either loads the raw (uncompressed) wave with 0x0054B004 when flag 8 is set and the entry has no INFO block, or decodes it with 0x00549FFC.
evidence: local flag byte set by 0x0065E340 is tested to choose 0x00549FFC (decoded) vs 0x0054B004 (raw); bit 8 of the caller flags is the 'raw only' request; called by 0x00549B7C and 0x0054A9FC; the wave-id + allocator pair matches the surrounding cache functions.

name: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecodedWithHeader
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecodedWithHeader(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, SoundAllocator* alloc, u32 size)
summary: Second half of the decoded-wave load path: looks the entry up, allocates space for a 0x2C-byte header plus one 4-byte word per channel, decodes the 0x2C-byte block with 0x0054B12C, then appends the per-channel offset table, writes the 'CIWV' trailer word and reports the buffer to the cache (vtable+8).
evidence: first decode asks for exactly 0x2C bytes and feeds it to 0x0065F420/0x0065F450 (the 0x2C-byte block accessors), second decode targets uVar4+uVar2, *(u32*)(uVar4+uVar2) = g_0054a3b4 (0x0073FF04, the CIWV trailer), then (**(code**)(*arg1+8))(arg1,waveId,buf) publishes it; only caller is 0x00549FFC.

name: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_PreloadGroup
signature: int maybe_Sound_WaveCache_PreloadGroup(SoundWaveCache* cache, int group, SoundAllocator* alloc)
summary: Preloads a whole group of waves: builds the group descriptor with 0x005493C0/0x0065EDC4 and then preloads every {id, size} pair in its table, aborting on the first failure. Returns 1 when the whole group is resident.
evidence: table layout *puVar1 = count, then {id, size} pairs read as puVar1[i*2+1], puVar1[i*2+2]; each entry goes through 0x0065E340 then 0x0054B004 or 0x00549FFC, i.e. exactly the two load flavours of this cache.

name: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_PreloadFromFile
signature: int maybe_Sound_WaveCache_PreloadFromFile(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 unused, u32 fileId, SoundAllocator* alloc)
summary: Opens a small descriptor file (0x0054B5A4 handle + 0x006604F8), reads a {waveId, size} pair out of it and preloads that single wave with 0x0054A170. Used for one-wave data blocks that are not part of a group table.
evidence: 0x006604F8 fills a {u32 id, u32 size} pair from the id given in arg3, the pair is then passed straight to 0x0054A170 with a flag word of 8; 0x0054B5A4 initialises the local reader handle.

name: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_LoadRaw
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_WaveCache_LoadRaw(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, SoundAllocator* alloc, u32 size, int publish)
summary: Loads an uncompressed wave: asks the cache for the entry size (0x0065E398), allocates it, copies the bytes with 0x0054B12C without decoding and, when publish is set (or the cache has no vtable publish hook), reports the buffer through vtable+8. Returns the buffer or 0.
evidence: Uses 0x0065E398 (the entry-size lookup that also feeds the decoded path) and 0x0054B12C with the decode-argument word 0; the bounds check 0x001180E0/0x001180F0 is the heap range test; 7 call sites, all in this cache family (0x00549B7C, 0x00549D10, 0x00549F18, 0x0054A170, 0x0054A8D0, 0x0054ABB0, 0x0054ADBC).

name: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_ReadBlocks
signature: int maybe_Sound_WaveCache_ReadBlocks(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, void* dst, int size, u32 param, int chunkLimit)
summary: Copies size bytes of a wave out of its archive: opens the archive stream for waveId (0x00542A00), sets the read parameter (vtable+0x40) and then loops over vtable+0x24 reads in chunkLimit-sized, 0x20-aligned pieces until the whole range is transferred. Returns size or -1.
evidence: 0x00542A00 Sound_Archive_OpenEntryStream (N_034); the transfer loop uses vtable+0x24 with a length rounded up as (len+0x1F)&~0x1F, i.e. a sector-aligned stream read; 0x00117E50/0x00117ED0 guard the whole transfer; retried when the size does not match (returns -1).

name: maybe_Sound_Command_FreeQueued
signature: void maybe_Sound_Command_FreeQueued(OsQueue* queue, u32 unused1, u32 unused2, u32 unused3)
summary: Drains a sound command queue down to the given mark, releasing every queued command with 0x00548800 and signalling the consumer side with 0x001166B4 through the queue object at queue+0xB4. Called from both sound driver tick variants to discard commands whose owner is gone.
evidence: walks with 0x0011C8E0 (the queue try-pop used elsewhere as Os_QueueTryPop) and 0x001166B4 (the same 'wake/commit' call that 0x0011B57C uses); the nodes come from 0x00548800, which sits immediately before the command executor 0x00548808.

name: Sound_Decoder_DestroyChannels
summary: Tears down a sound decoder's two channel arrays: destroys the 32-entry table at self+0x34 and the 33-entry table at self+0xB4 (the 3DS DSP channel counts) and clears the 'initialised' byte at +0x18D. Mirror image of the setup done by Sound_Decoder_Init.
evidence: mirrors 0x0054B608 Sound_Decoder_Init (N_007: same +0x34/+0xB4 arrays of 0x20 and 0x21 entries, sets +0x18D=1); here both are handed to 0x0012032C (destroy/finalise) and +0x18D is cleared; only caller is 0x00542580, the sound driver teardown.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_SetupStreams
summary: Applies a playback mode to every DSP stream of a voice: stores the mode byte (modeParam[0]) at voice+0x50, then for each of the voice's stream handles enables it, maps the mode to the stream output type (0/2/1) and forwards the extra parameter and the global output mode to the low-level stream API.
evidence: voice->f_8 is the stream count and voice+i*4 the stream handles (same layout as every other function in this block); the per-stream calls 0x0051A1CC/0x0051A1EC/0x00519F94/0x0051A3A4 are the codec-stream setters also used by maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_Start (0x004FCF9C); the global at 0x007E7268 holds the output mode byte at +2; tail resets the four state bytes +0x15..+0x18.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_SetPauseMode
summary: Puts a voice into the requested pause state: stores mode at voice+0x40, re-registers the voice with the mixer (0x00550B78/0x00550CD4) and, when mode==1, enables the per-stream pause flag on all streams.
evidence: +0x40 is the same 'pause/stop' field read by 0x0054D4B4 and 0x0054CBB4; 0x0051893C(stream,1) is the per-stream pause setter used together with 0x0054D25C in the stop path; queue handle from 0x00550B78 (the mixer queue).

name: Sound_Mixer_BuildVolumeMatrix
signature: void Sound_Mixer_BuildVolumeMatrix(SoundVoice* voice, int speaker, float* out12)
summary: Builds the 12-float (3 rows x 4 columns) per-speaker volume matrix for a voice: clamps the three surround gains at +0x44/+0x48/+0x4C to 0..1, derives the channel enable mask from the speaker mode at +0x2D (1..8), then combines the pan/cross-feed terms with the output mode from the global settings block.
evidence: clamps against g_0054cba4=1.0f and g_0054cba8=0.0f, switch on voice->f_2d producing three 0/1/2-byte speaker masks, and the result is exactly 12 floats (out[0..0xB]) fed to 0x00519D24; the caller 0x0054D6A4 applies one matrix per stream, so this is the mixer's pan matrix; +0x2c selects mono/stereo and +0x30 the per-side pan.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_NotifyFinished
summary: Completion poll for a voice: when the voice is active, the 'armed' byte at +0x16 is set and the current stream has left the running states, it invokes the stored callback (voice+0xC) with reason 0 and clears the armed/active bytes.
evidence: condition (voice->f_1c->f_11 != 1 && != 2) uses the same stream state byte as 0x0055624C and the 0x51Axxx stream API; callback is (*(code*)voice[3])(voice, 0, voice[4]); clears +0x16 and +0x15, the two 'pending callback' bytes also cleared by 0x0054CE70/0x0054CEC0.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_SetOutputMode
summary: Sets the output routing mode of a voice: forwards mode to every stream (0x0051A388) and records it at voice+0x23. Used together with the mute/loop setters right before a voice is started.
evidence: same per-stream loop as 0x0054CD84/0x0054CE30 but a different stream setter (0x0051A388); the mode is also stored at +0x23 which 0x0054C8A4 reads as the 'output mode' byte for the pan matrix; callers are 0x0054E88C (start note), 0x0054FE18 and 0x00552914.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_SetStreamMute
summary: Applies a 0/1/2 mute-or-solo state to every stream of a voice by calling 0x0051A3A4 on each handle; any other value is normalised to 0.
evidence: identical per-stream loop to 0x0054CC2C/0x0054CE30 but with the 0x0051A3A4 stream setter; the same 0/1/2 mapping appears in 0x0054C664 (uVar2 = 0/1/2) and 0x005561BC passes voice+0x197 into it.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_SetStreamLoopFlag
summary: Forwards a flag to every stream of a voice through 0x0051A3D8 (the third per-stream boolean setter); used by the sequence note start to mark a voice as looping.
evidence: per-stream loop over voice->f_8 handles calling 0x0051A3D8, the sibling of 0x0051A388/0x0051A3A4/0x0051A4AC which 0x0054CC2C/0x0054CD84/0x0054D25C use; only caller is 0x00552914 (multi-voice note start).

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_ReleaseToPool
summary: Returns a finished voice to the pool: clears the stream count, the state bytes and the callback owner, unlinks it from the mixer list (0x00550B78/0x00550EA4) and calls the owner callback with reason 3 (released).
evidence: sets *voice=0, +0x17/+0x15=0, voice[2]=0, +0x14=0 and calls the callback as (cb)(voice,3,voice[4]) - the same '3' the mixer-side 0x00550D94/0x00550E04 use when they tear a voice down; 0x00550EA4 unlinks from the list at queue+0x10.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_DetachStreams
summary: Detaches a voice from its streams: when the voice is not in the 'deferred' state it stops and frees every stream except keep and zeroes the array, otherwise it only nulls the entry for keep and flags +0x1B; then it clears the voice state, unlinks it from the mixer list and calls the owner callback with reason 3.
evidence: pairs 0x0051A4AC (stop) with 0x00519BE4 (free) per stream; the branch on +0x1A/+0x1B is the same deferred-release flag pair used by 0x0054D4B4; final block is identical in shape to 0x0054CE70.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_ApplyPendingParams
summary: Flushes the voice's dirty parameter bits onto its streams: bit 4 re-sends the stream parameters, bit 0x40 re-sends the mixing matrix, bit 8 rebuilds the volume matrix (0x0054D6A4), bit 0x10 applies the resample flag when the effective sample rate is below 16000 Hz, and bit 0x20 pushes the 3D positional parameters from the owning camera/listener object.
evidence: five independent 'if (f_20 & bit)' blocks, each clearing its bit after the update, over the voice's stream array; bit 0x10 compares 0x0054C07C (current sample rate) against 16000; bit 0x20 reads the listener object at g_007E7268->+0x74 indexed by voice+0x22 and calls its vtable+8 to obtain 3 floats; called from the per-frame voice walk 0x00550C3C.

name: Sound_Voice_StopStreams
summary: Stops a voice: if it is currently running (+0x16) it calls the per-stream stop 0x0051A4AC with 1 on every stream, then clears the running/playing/deferred bytes +0x16/+0x18/+0x17/+0x15.
evidence: 7 call sites, all teardown paths (0x00550A0C pool free, 0x00550D94/0x00550E04, 0x00553EEC, 0x0055614C, 0x0055624C, 0x0055668C); 0x0051A4AC is the per-stream stop-and-release used with 0x00519BE4.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_UpdatePlayState
signature: void maybe_Sound_Voice_UpdatePlayState(SoundVoice* voice, u32 streamIndex, u32 unused)
summary: Play/pause state machine for one voice: starts the streams on the first call (0x00518A1C, volume matrix, mixer register, 0x0051A544), then applies state 0/1/2 to every stream via 0x0051A4AC depending on the pause and deferred bits at +0x20.
evidence: three-way tail: i==1 -> 0x0051A4AC(x,0) play, i==2 -> (x,1) pause, i==3 -> (x,2) stop; the start block is the exact sequence (volume matrix, 0x006615F8 mixer hook, 0x0051A544) used by 0x0054CFA8 bit 0x40; called from 0x00550C3C once per frame per voice.

name: Sound_Voice_UpdateVolumes
summary: Recomputes and pushes the per-stream volume matrix: for each stream it builds the 3x4 matrix for that speaker index with 0x0054C8A4 and hands it to the stream with 0x00519D24.
evidence: zeroes twelve locals, loops i over voice->f_8, calls 0x0054C8A4(voice, i, &matrix) then 0x00519D24(stream, &matrix); called by 0x0054CFA8 (dirty bit 8) and 0x0054D4B4 (start), i.e. exactly the two places a mixer would recompute gains.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_ReleaseStreamPair
summary: Releases the two stream slots of a voice with 0x00519BE4 and returns the voice, leaving the pointers in place (the caller is expected to drop the voice immediately afterwards).
evidence: fixed loop of 2 over *(int*)(voice+i*4) calling 0x00519BE4, the stream free used by 0x0054CEC0; only caller is 0x00550E04, the voice-list shutdown.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_TickWithProfiling
summary: One frame of the sound driver, with profiling: when timing is enabled it appends the current tick to the 8-byte-record ring at +0x1B8 and calls 0x0054DAA4 to accumulate frame statistics, then (under the driver lock) runs the two intrusive lists of pending objects, drains the completed-request queues and ticks the mixer and sequence-player subsystems.
evidence: exact superset of 0x0054D93C (identical body minus the +0x1B8 ring append and the 0x0054DAA4 call), which is the classic dev/release twin pattern; the two lists at +0x1D4/+0x1E0 are circular lists with vtable calls at +8/+0xC/+0x10; the subsystem tick set is 0x0054F880 (sequence), 0x0054B664/0x0054B6B0 (command queues), 0x0054EF90/0x0054EFEC (voices), 0x0054C050, 0x00550B78/0x00550C3C (mixer).

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_Tick
summary: One frame of the sound driver without the profiling capture: unlinks and destroys the pending objects on the two driver lists, drains the command queues, then ticks the voice, mixer and sequence-player subsystems.
evidence: byte-for-byte the same call sequence as 0x0054D8C0 minus the tick-ring append and the 0x0054DAA4 statistics call; both take the same driver object (locks at +0x1C4, lists at +0x1D4/+0x1E0, flag +0x1F6).

name: Sound_Profile_RecordFrame
summary: Accumulates one frame of sound-thread timing: adds the 64-bit tick delta and a sub-counter to the running totals at +0/+4/+0x18, converts the delta to a float load figure (0.02 scale, clamped to 0..100), tracks a maximum, fills a 101-bucket histogram and, when a capture buffer is installed, appends a {float, byte, byte} record.
evidence: g_0054dcc0=-0.00161 / g_0054dccc=0.0204 / g_0054dcd4=100.0 constants, `if (iVar6 < 0x65)` bounds the histogram to 101 entries, record stride 8 at arg1[0x7E] with +0x80/+0x81 cursors; only caller is the profiling driver tick 0x0054D8C0; 0x00124ACC is the unsigned-to-float conversion.

name: maybe_Sound_Profile_SetBuffer
signature: void maybe_Sound_Profile_SetBuffer(SoundDriver* driver, u32* records, u32 count)
summary: Installs the profiling record ring: under the driver lock it stores the buffer and capacity and resets the write cursor, but only when the driver is in the recording state; otherwise it just releases the lock.
evidence: writes +0x1B8 (buffer), +0x1BC (capacity), +0x1C0 (cursor) - the exact fields 0x0054D8C0 and 0x0054DAA4 use; guarded by +0x1F6==1; the lock is the same +0x1C4 monitor.

name: maybe_Sound_Profile_ClearBuffer
summary: Detaches the profiling record ring from the sound driver (buffer, capacity and cursor set to zero) under the driver lock, so a freed buffer is never written again.
evidence: clears +0x1B8/+0x1BC/+0x1C0 which 0x0054DCD8 installs and 0x0054DAA4 writes; called from the driver teardown 0x00542580.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_AddDeferredRelease
summary: Appends an object to the driver's deferred-release list at +0x1D0/+0x1D4 under the driver lock, so it is destroyed on the next frame instead of in the caller's context.
evidence: 0x0011FCF8(driver+0x1D0, driver+0x1D4, object+4) is the same intrusive-list append the fs request queue uses, wrapped in the +0x1C4 monitor; the list is drained by 0x0054D8C0/0x0054D93C with vtable+8/+0xC; callers are the archive-close paths 0x00543CFC/0x005440CC.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_RemoveDeferredRelease
summary: Removes an object from the driver's deferred-release list under the driver lock, cancelling a pending destroy. Counterpart of 0x0054DED0 and only used when the object is re-registered before the next frame.
evidence: 0x0011FCBC(driver+0x1D0, object+4) is the intrusive-list remove paired with the 0x0011FCF8 append in 0x0054DED0; caller 0x00546220 is the archive reopen path.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_StopTimer
summary: Stops the driver's periodic timer once: if the +0x1F4 flag is set it raises +0x1F7, calls 0x00517A60 (timer stop) and clears the flag.
evidence: the same flag/call pair appears in 0x0054DF60 immediately after; 0x00517A38/0x00517A60 are the tick-source start/stop pair (0x00517A38 is used to read the current tick in 0x0054D8C0); only caller is the driver teardown 0x00542580.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_ShutdownHooks
summary: Final driver shutdown step: stops the periodic timer, walks the second deferred list calling vtable+0x10 (finalise) on each node and marks the driver as closed (+0x1CC = -1).
evidence: same +0x1F4/+0x1F7 timer block as 0x0054DF34, then a circular-list walk over driver+0x1E0 using vtable+0x10 and finally +0x1CC = 0xFFFFFFFF; called from the driver teardown 0x00542580.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqChannel_Tick
summary: Per-frame step of one sequence channel: advances the five envelope/fade counters (+0x8C..+0xA6) towards their targets, counts down the remaining-length counter at +0x7C and, while a note is still held, keeps calling the channel's own vtable slot 1 (up to 10000 iterations) to feed the next note event. Returns 1 while alive, -1 when a sub-step reports end and 0 when the channel is idle.
evidence: g_0054e25c = 0x2710 (10000) caps the inner loop; the five counter pairs (+0x8C/+0x8E, +0x94/+0x96, +0x98/+0x9A, +0xA0/+0xA2, +0xA4/+0xA6) are the same envelope fields interpolated in 0x0054E37C; (**(code**)(*self+8)) is vtable slot 1 of the class whose slot 0 is 0x0054EBA4 (channel vtable 0x0073D2E8); the +0x7C countdown is also decremented by 0x0054E790.

name: Sound_SeqChannel_KillNotes
summary: Hard-kills every note still owned by a sequence channel (0x00555DA4 on each element of the list at +0x130) and empties the list.
evidence: single walk of the +0x130 singly linked list through note+0x1AC calling 0x00555DA4 (the note-free helper also used by 0x0054E828, 0x0054EBA4, 0x0054EE94); callers are the channel tick paths and the sequencer shutdown.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqChannel_StopNotes
summary: Fades out and releases every playing note of a channel: first recomputes the channel parameters (0x0054E37C), then for each playing note optionally forces the volume (0x00547134) and finishes it (0x00556648).
evidence: iterates the +0x130 list, tests note->f_139 ('playing'), applies 0x00547134(&note->f_98, volume & 0xFF) then 0x00556648(note); 0x00556648 sets note state 4 = finished; same pattern as 0x0054E828/0x0054EBA4.

name: Sound_SeqChannel_ApplyMixParams
summary: Propagates the sequencer's current mix parameters onto every note of this channel: interpolates the five envelope pairs, scales the channel volume/expression/pan (0..127 and 0..255 values) by the sequencer's track gains, folds in the key-shift/pitch terms and writes the resulting per-note values (+0xB4..+0x160) before each note is re-mixed.
evidence: 1/128, 1/127 and 1/63 scale constants (g_0054e6f8=0.0078125, g_0054e710=0.00787402, g_0054e6fc=0.015873) convert 0..127 / 0..255 MIDI-style values to floats; reads the sequencer through *(int*)(self+300) (+0x12C) including its f_14/f_18/f_1c/f_24/f_2c/f_60/f_79/f_7C; the loop over the +0x130 list writes note offsets +0x140..+0x160; called from 0x0054E328/0x0054E828/0x0054EBA4/0x0054EE94/0x00555308.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqChannel_UpdateNoteTimeouts
summary: Decrements the per-note duration counter at note+0x190 and finishes the note when it reaches zero (unless the note is already in state 4), then refreshes each note's gate flag.
evidence: note+400 == +0x190 is decremented and compared with 0; 0x005565F8 (note finish) is called from this path; 0x00555E18(note,1) is the per-note gate refresh; walks the +0x130 list.

name: Sound_SeqChannel_Stop
summary: Stops a sequence channel completely: recomputes parameters, finishes every playing note, then frees all notes with 0x00555DA4, clears the note list and the +5 'active' byte.
evidence: 0x0054E37C + 0x00556648 + 0x00555DA4 in that order, then self->f_130 = 0 and *(u8*)(self+5) = 0; called from 0x005549EC, 0x00554C34 and 0x00555878, all sequencer shutdown/rewind paths.

name: Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote
signature: int Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote(SoundSeqChannel* channel, int note, int velocity, u32 duration, int reuse)
summary: Starts one note on a sequence channel: converts note+velocity to a pitch/period word, reuses a finished note in the +0x130 list or allocates a new one from the voice pool (0x005552D0), applies volume/pan/tie parameters, computes the note's sample length, links it at the head of the list and sets up its streams (0x0054C75C/0x0054C82C/0x0054CC2C). Returns the note object or 0.
evidence: g_0054eb90 is the fixed-point constant that converts (channel->f_F0 * velocity) to a period; result->f_194 = note number and 0x00555D8C stores the pitch; prepends with note->f_1AC = self->f_130; self->f_130 = note; allocation via 0x005552D0; called from the sequencer note-on thunk 0x006626D8.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqChannel_SetPauseMode
summary: Virtual slot 0 of the sequence-channel class: mode 0/1 sets the pause byte at +0x7A, mode 2 stops all notes gracefully (finish then free), mode 3 frees the notes and releases their voices, and modes 2/3 empty the note list.
evidence: first entry of the 16-entry channel vtable at 0x0073D2E8 ({func,0} pairs, slot 0 = 0x0054EBA4) that the sound command dispatcher installs on the 16 channel objects at sequencer+0x90; the mode semantics match 0x0054E828 / 0x0055614C; no direct caller because it is only invoked virtually.

name: Sound_SeqChannel_Dtor
summary: Destructor for a sequence channel: installs the base vtable (0x00781B34), recomputes parameters, finishes and frees all notes and marks the channel inactive. Returns the object for the deleting-destructor convention.
evidence: stores g_0054ef08 = 0x00781B34 as the first word (vtable install), then the stop sequence of 0x0054E828 reduces to finish (0x00556648) + free (0x00555DA4) + list clear + +5 = 0; returns its argument, the ARM deleting-dtor pattern.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_ReleaseAllChannels
summary: Releases every sequence channel owned by the driver: walks the intrusive list at driver+8 and calls 0x0055624C(channel, 1) on each node (node = list pointer - 0x1B0 bytes).
evidence: circular-list walk over *(int**)(arg1+8) with nodes at piVar1-0x6C ints, calling 0x0055624C with mode 1; called from both driver tick variants.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_ReleaseAllSeqChannels
summary: Releases every sequence channel bound to the driver when the +0x10 flag says the subsystem is running: 0x0055614C on each list node followed by one 0x00556C04 pool release, then clears the flag.
evidence: same node geometry as 0x0054EFEC (list at +8, nodes at -0x6C ints) but calling 0x0055614C (note release) plus 0x00556C04 at the end; only caller is the sound driver teardown 0x00542580.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_SetSlotTimer
signature: void maybe_Sound_Player_SetSlotTimer(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, int ticks)
summary: Stops one of the player's two playback slots and re-arms its timer: with ticks==0 the slot is stopped and the alarm cleared, otherwise the alarm at slot+0x14 is set from the tick count so the slot fires again later.
evidence: slot base = player + slot*0x10, the 0x10-stride block whose +0x14/+0x18 and +0x1C/+0x20 pairs 0x0054F880 interpolates; 0x006EF854 is the per-slot alarm setter (called with 0 to cancel here); dispatcher opcode 0x9.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_StartSlotTrack
signature: int maybe_Sound_Player_StartSlotTrack(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 trackId, u32 param)
summary: Binds a track to one of the player's two slots: refuses when the slot is already busy, stops the previous track and clears its alarm, then registers trackId (0x005164FC), applies the extra parameter (0x005166E4) and starts it (0x0051658C). Returns 1 on success.
evidence: guard on slot+0x294 (the slot's track-handle byte) and the same +0x1C/+0x20 pair as 0x0054F880; 0x005164FC/0x005166E4/0x0051658C are the track start/param/play triplet; slot+0x290 receives the handle; the +0x6C/+0x70/+0x74 fields belong to the same object as 0x0054FDD0/0x0054FE18.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackA
signature: int maybe_Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackA(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 trackId, u32 param)

evidence: same prologue as 0x0054F2EC; g_00519c04 = 0x007EF3C4 and the slot record is trackList + slot*8 with +0x34/+0x38 handle fields; 0x005185E4(g_005176f0 = 0x007F2C3C, slot, 0/1, ...) notifies the global track table; dispatcher opcode 0x5.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackB
signature: int maybe_Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackB(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 trackId, u32 param)
summary: Variant of the slot track start for the second track list (0x007EF3C4 + 0x44): detaches the previous track and registers the new one with 0x00519674, then notifies the global track table.
evidence: byte-for-byte the shape of 0x0054F48C but using g_00519c18 = 0x007EF3C4 and the +0x38 handle plus 0x00519674 instead of the +0x34/0x00519490 pair; dispatcher opcode 0x6.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_SetSlotCallback
signature: int maybe_Sound_Player_SetSlotCallback(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 callback)
summary: Installs the per-slot completion callback: stops the slot, clears its alarm and, when the slot has no handler yet, registers 0x0054F7C0 as the default handler with 0x00518750, then stores the user callback in the slot's wait list.
evidence: g_0054f5f0 = 0x0054F7C0 is stored as the default handler through 0x00518750(slot, handler, slot); the slot's 0xC-stride list head at +0x54 is filled with 0x0011FCF8; dispatcher opcode 0x4.

name: Sound_Player_StopSlot
summary: Stops everything running on one playback slot: stops and notifies the slot's two sub-tracks (0x00516618/0x0051698C), releases the note list at slot+0x54 through 0x005182BC/0x0051CF4C and clears the slot's +0x280/+0x284 state.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_TickSlots
summary: Per-frame tick of the player's two slots: advances the two envelope ramps (+0x34..+0x38 and +0x14..+0x18) and their duration counters, pushes the interpolated volume with 0x0051871C, reaps finished track handles at +0x290, and finally advances the +0xC/+0x10 prefetch counters, signalling the consumer queue (0x00550D48) when a slot actually ran.
evidence: exactly two slots (loop `if (1 < (int)uVar9)`), 0x10-byte stride, 1.0f/0.0f clamp constants, track-handle byte +0x294 tested == 2 and released through 0x005164B4/0x00516860; 0x00550B78/0x00550D48 is the same queue pair the command executor uses; called from both driver tick variants.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_StopAllSlots
summary: Stops both playback slots and hands their track handles back (0x00518750), clearing the two 4-byte track arrays at +0x6C and +0x274 and then the 'open' byte.
evidence: loop of 2 over the same slots as 0x0054F880, calling 0x0054F6D0(slot) then 0x00518750(slot, +0x6C[i], +0x274[i]) and zeroing both arrays; only caller is the sound driver teardown 0x00542580.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_SetParams
signature: void maybe_Sound_Player_SetParams(SoundPlayer* player, u32* params, u32* volumes)
summary: Applies a parameter block to a player: stores the three words at +0x6C/+0x70/+0x74 and the six volume words at +0xAC..+0xC0, marks the player ready and registers it with the mixer (0x0054DEBC).
evidence: +0x6C/+0x70/+0x74 are exactly the fields read by 0x0054FE18 as wave id / mode / duration, and +0xAC..+0xC0 are the six words 0x00550254 copies into the fetch descriptor; +0xA0/+0xA2 are the state/registered byte pair; 0x0054D868 returns the driver; dispatcher opcode 0x23.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_StartWave
summary: Starts playing the wave described by the player: opens the CWAV (0x0054944C), reads its wave-info block (0x0065EF6C), computes the start window from the player's +0x70/+0x74 fields, allocates a note from the voice pool (0x00555E38), copies the PCM (0x006605B4), applies volume/pan and starts playback with 0x005561BC.
evidence: 0x0054944C Sound_Cwav_Open then 0x0065EF6C (INFO-block field reader) then 0x00555E38 (note alloc with callback 0x005501A8) then 0x006605B4 (PCM setup) then 0x005561BC (start); the +0x70==1 branch scales +0x74 by local_90/1000, i.e. a fade or loop time; called from 0x00550254.

name: Sound_Player_UpdateVolumePan
summary: Per-frame update of a playing wave: converts the 0..127 / 0..64 volume and pan fields at +0x91..+0x98 (with the +0x2C override) into the four float gains, applies the surround offsets and pushes them to the note together with the position block.
evidence: 1/127, 1/128 and 1/64 scale constants convert the stored 0x40-centred values to floats; writes note->f_140/f_144/f_148/f_14C/f_150 and the 4-word position at +0xB4; uses 0x0054C75C/0x0054C82C (per-channel volume setters) and 0x00555ED8/0x00555DBC; callers 0x00550254/0x0055058C.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_Update
summary: State machine that turns a pending play request into a playing note: state 1 opens the file asynchronously (0x005421C0/0x00547644), state 2 waits for the read to finish (0x00547FB0/0x00547EB0), and once the data is ready it records the result and calls 0x0054FE18 to start playback, or 0x0054FF74 to update a running one.
evidence: three explicit states in +0xA0 (1/2/3) with early returns, the fs request calls 0x005421C0/0x00547644/0x00547EB0/0x00547FB0 that 0x005514CC and 0x00555308 also use, and the +0xA8 request object whose +0x3C is the opened stream; transitions are driven by 0x0054FE18's return value.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_Play
signature: void maybe_Sound_Player_Play(SoundPlayer* player, u32* params, u32* waveRef)
summary: Queues a sound file for playback: aborts any current request, stores the new parameter words (+0x6C/+0x70/+0x74) and the wave reference (+0x64/+0x68/+0x5F), sets state 3 and registers the object with the driver queue (0x00555B9C/0x00555BF0) and the mixer list (0x0054DEBC).
evidence: writes exactly the fields 0x0054FE18 reads (wave id at +0x68, mode +0x70, duration +0x74, +0x5F, +0x64), sets +0xA0=3 / +0xC=1, and is opcode 0x22 in the sound command dispatcher; the cancel-first block is identical to 0x0055058C.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_Stop
summary: Stops and cancels a player: unregisters it from the driver queue, finishes and frees the note if one is playing (0x0054FF74/0x00556648/0x00555DA4), clears the active flag, releases the pending fs request at +0xA8 and detaches the driver-registry node.
evidence: mirror image of 0x005504D0 (same +0x44 queue node, +0x9C note, +0xA8 request); 0x0011E5C4 tests the request state byte before either releasing the buffer chain (+0x20) or cancelling the archive stream (+0x14/+0x18) with 0x0054218C; called from 0x00550744.

name: maybe_Sound_Player_Ctor
summary: Constructs a player in place: links the two intrusive-list nodes to the driver (+0x30 and +0x44), runs the stop/init pass and installs the player vtable 0x00781BD0. Returns the player.
evidence: arg1[0x11] = driver+0x30 and arg1[0x14] = driver+0x44 set the two list hooks, *arg1 = driver then *arg1 = g_0055077c = 0x00781BD0 (vtable install after the base init), with 0x0055058C in between; same constructor shape as 0x00555B60.

name: Sound_Mixer_TickVoices
summary: Per-frame walk over every active mixer voice in three passes: completion poll (0x0054CBB4), pending-parameter flush (0x0054CFA8) and play/pause state update (0x0054D4B4). Called from both driver tick variants.
evidence: three separate full walks of the circular voice list at mixer+8 with nodes at -0x16 ints (= -0x58 bytes), exactly the voice header size used by 0x00550A0C/0x00550D94; the three callees are the voice helpers defined in this batch.

name: maybe_Sound_Mixer_PopFinishedVoice
summary: Tries to reclaim a finished voice: if the mixer has a voice list and the head voice's priority is not above the requested one, it stops and frees that voice, invokes its owner callback with reason 2 and returns the freed slot value; otherwise returns 0.
evidence: reads the voice header at list -0x58 (priority at -0x18, owner value at -0x50, callback at -0x4C), then 0x0054D25C (stop) + 0x0054D1F4 (free) and finally (cb)(voice,2,ctx) - the '2' reason also used by 0x00550A0C when it reclaims a slot.

name: maybe_Sound_Mixer_ShutdownVoices
summary: Shuts down a mixer's voices: repeatedly stops the active-list head (callback reason 1) and frees finished-list entries with 0x0054D834 until both lists are empty, then clears the mixer's 'open' byte.
evidence: two drain loops over mixer+4 (active) and mixer+0x10 (finished) using the same voice header offsets as 0x00550D94 and calling 0x0054D834 (release stream pair); tail clears *self; called from the sound driver teardown 0x00542580.

name: maybe_Sound_Mixer_RelinkVoice
summary: Moves a voice between the mixer's two intrusive lists (deferred at +4, active at +0x10/+0x14) in one step, used when a voice is released or re-registered while the mixer is being walked.
evidence: 0x0011FCBC(mixer+4, voice+0x58) removes the node and 0x0011FCF8(mixer+0x10, mixer+0x14, voice+0x58) appends it to the other list; callers are 0x0054CE70, 0x0054CEC0 and 0x0054D1F4, i.e. the voice release paths.

name: maybe_Sound_Stream_CancelWorkByOwnerA
summary: Cancels every pending sound-stream work item owned by `owner`: under the sound stream context lock it walks the three work lanes (0xC stride) and, for each node whose owner field matches, unlinks it, marks it cancelled (state 4) and releases its wait object.
evidence: identical to the copy at 0x005480C4 that N_034 named maybe_Sound_Stream_CancelWorkByOwner; 0x00547FB0 returns the stream context and +0x2C is its monitor; three lanes indexed `i < 3` with 0xC stride; node->f_14 == owner is the match; state byte set to 4 and 0x00111D50 releases the wait object. The build ships three copies of this helper (0x005480C4, 0x005514B4, 0x00551B58).

name: maybe_Sound_Stream_QueueWorkItem
signature: void maybe_Sound_Stream_QueueWorkItem(SoundPlayer* player, u32* channels, u32 offset, u32 length, u32 param, u8 priority, u8 flags)
summary: Queues an asynchronous sound-data read: allocates a 0x58-byte work item from the player's stream handle (0x00556C48), zero-fills it, installs the work-item vtable (0x00781C08), stores offset/length/param and the per-channel destination pointers, links the completion callback into the player's list and posts the item to the stream work queue (0x00547EB0).
evidence: 0x00116AE0 zero-fill of 0x58 bytes, *puVar5 = g_005515dc = 0x00781C08 (vtable), the destination array is filled from arg2 up to player->f_20 entries, puVar5->f_14 is linked into player+0x84/+0x88 with 0x0011FCF8, then 0x00547FB0 (stream context) + 0x00547EB0 maybe_Sound_Stream_QueueWorkLane (N_034) posts it; callers 0x00552914 and 0x00552E3C.

name: maybe_Sound_Stream_CancelWorkByOwnerB
summary: Second copy of the fs request canceller: identical to 0x005514B4 (walk the three request lists, unlink and cancel every node owned by `owner`). The build ships the same helper twice for two call sites.
evidence: instruction-for-instruction duplicate of 0x005514B4 (and of N_034's maybe_Sound_Stream_CancelWorkByOwner at 0x005480C4): same context, +0x2C monitor, three lanes, 0xC stride, state byte 4; the only difference is the caller (0x00547D54 maybe_Sound_Stream_OnEnd instead of 0x00553EEC).

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote(SoundSeqPlayer* player, int restart, int outSlots, u32 expectedId)
summary: Starts a note that fans out to several voices: validates the player against the expected id, optionally restarts it, allocates up to 8 voice slots from the mixer (0x00550940/0x00550A0C with priority 0x7FFF and callback 0x0055389C), submits one read per slot (0x005514CC) and arms the per-channel mute/loop flags afterwards.
evidence: loop bound player[0x2D] clamped to 8 -> player[0x88]; 0x00550940/0x00550900 allocate and release the per-slot buffers, 0x00550A0C(count, priority=0x7FFF, ..., 0x0055389C, &slot) is the voice-pool allocator, 0x005514CC submits the per-slot read; the tail applies 0x0054CC2C/0x0054CE30 (output mode and loop flag) per channel; dispatcher opcode '*'.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_UpdateActiveNotes
signature: void maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_UpdateActiveNotes(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 frame, u32 arg3, u32 source)
summary: Processes the player's active note table: while the next entry is in the 'ready' state it consumes it, accumulates the per-entry sample offset, refreshes the per-channel volumes from the source object (0x00518820) and starts the next batch of voices through the same read path the note starter uses.
evidence: entry stride 0x18 at player+f_70*0x18 with state byte +0x241 == 3; per-channel offsets at player+i*0x3C8+0x228 and count player+0x220; uses 0x006615C4 (voice/note state test), 0x00518820 and 0x0054D450; the shared 0x00125E58 (std_UInt64Divide) converts the tempo to samples; no direct caller - reached through the player vtable.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_StopVoices
summary: Stops every voice belonging to a sequence player: cancels the pending fs requests of the player handle, stops each of the player+0x220 channel voices (0x0054D25C) and unregisters the player from the driver queue.
evidence: 0x005514B4(player->f_60) cancels the fs requests, the loop over player+0x220 with voice pointers at player+i*0x3C8+0x22C calls 0x0054D25C, then 0x0054D868/0x0011FCB0 unlinks the +0x44 queue node; same queue-node geometry as 0x0054FF74/0x0055058C.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_ApplyChannelMap
summary: Applies the player's channel map to the hardware voices: for each of the player+0x224 entries with a non-zero channel count it configures the voice streams (0x0054C664) and starts them (0x0054D470), then registers the player with the driver queue.
evidence: outer loop over +0x224 records of stride 0x24 with count at +0x2074 and handles at +0x2068; per handle 0x0054C664(stream, mode, 0) + 0x0054D470 (the stream setup/start pair 0x005561BC also uses); tail uses 0x0054D868/0x0054DEBC to register.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_InitFromParam
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_InitFromParam(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u8* param, u32 driver)
summary: Initialises a sequence player from a parameter block: stores the driver handle, the mode byte and the value at param+4, takes the next sequence id from the global counter 0x007AED00, publishes the player into the driver's sequence record (+0x10/+0x18/+0x1C/+0x24/+0x26/+0x28/+0x2C) and opens it (0x00547E7C). Returns 1.
evidence: g_00554468 = 0x007AED00 is a u16 counter incremented per player and stored at player+0x21F8 and at driverRecord+0x24; the driver record fields written are read back by 0x0054E37C through *(int*)(self+300); 0x00547E7C maybe_Sound_Stream_QueueWork (N_034) starts the stream read.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_ComputeTempoStep
summary: Converts the player's tempo/tick fields into the next step length: multiplies the two 16-bit tempo values by the 1/60000 sample constant, performs the 64-bit fixed-point division and stores the resulting tick counts used to advance the sequence.
evidence: g_00554bb0 = 1.66667e-05 = 1/60000 (BPM -> samples), g_00554bbc = 2.68112e+08 and g_00554bb8 = 0x4E200000 (= 671088640 = 10*2^26) are the fixed-point scale/limit, 0x00723EA8 is the 64-bit divide; reads player->f_75/f_76 (the tempo pair) and player+0x64; called from 0x00555308 and 0x00555878.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetParamBlock
signature: void maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetParamBlock(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32* triple, u32* block13)
summary: Stores the 3+13 word parameter block carried by sound command 0x0E: three words into +0x168/+0x16C/+0x170 and thirteen into +0x17C..+0x1AC (two 4-word vectors plus five 2-word pairs), then registers the player with the mixer.
evidence: writes +0x168..+0x1AC contiguously from arg2[0..2] and arg3[0..0xC], then 0x0054D868/0x0054DEBC; the payload layout is byte-for-byte what 0x00548F90 fills into a 0x0E command and the dispatcher routes 0x0E here.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_ReleaseChannels
summary: Releases all 16 sequence channels of a player: unlinks the pending queue node, then for each of the 16 channel pointers at player+0x90 stops the channel (0x0054E828) and destroys it through its owner vtable (slot 0xC), clearing the slot.
evidence: fixed loop of 16 over *(int*)(self+i*4+0x90) - the array 0x005551F8 fills and 0x00554CB0 walks - calling 0x0054E828 then (**(code**)(*owner+0xC)) and nulling the entry; 5 callers, all shutdown paths (0x005549EC, 0x00555308, 0x005556A0, 0x00555794, 0x00555878).

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_CallChannelsSlot0
signature: void maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_CallChannelsSlot0(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, u32 value)
summary: Calls virtual slot 0 (0x0054EBA4, pause/stop mode) on every channel selected by a 16-bit channel mask, passing one argument. This is the mechanical 'broadcast one value to selected channels' helper behind sound command 0x16.
evidence: g_00554d30 = 0x0073D2E8 is the channel vtable ({func,0} pairs, slot 0 = 0x0054EBA4); the loop shifts arg2 right and uses bit 0 to select player+0x90+i*4; the same 16-entry mask walk appears in 0x00554DC0/0x00554E80/0x00554F1C/0x00554FB8/0x00555048 with different vtable slots.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_FadeChannelNotes
signature: void maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_FadeChannelNotes(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, u32 a, u32 b)
summary: Broadcasts a note fade to every channel selected by the mask: virtual slot 1 (0x0054E084) stores the on/off byte at channel+0x7B and then, for every note of that channel, sets the fade target to 0x00 (when the byte is non-zero) or 0xFF and the fade length from the second argument.
evidence: slot 1 of the channel vtable 0x0073D2E8 = 0x0054E084, whose body sets self->f_7B = arg2 and then walks the note list at +0x130 writing note+0x180/+0x181 (current/target volume) and note+0x182/+0x184 (fade length/position); the fade length is (arg3+4) scaled by g_0054e114; dispatcher opcode 0x17.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelField83
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelField83(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, int index)
summary: Guarded broadcast of a byte to the masked channels: returns 0 when the per-index enable byte at player+index*0xC+0x13C is clear, otherwise calls virtual slot 9, which stores the byte at channel+0x83, and returns 1.
evidence: slot 9 of vtable 0x0073D2E8 (+0x48) = 0x0054E120, whose assembly is `strb r1,[r0,#0x83]; bx lr`; the guard byte player+arg3*0xC+0x13C is the same 0xC-stride channel state table used by 0x0054F554; dispatcher opcode 0x1F.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFieldF4
signature: void maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFieldF4(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, u32 value)
summary: Broadcasts one byte to every masked channel through virtual slot 10 of the channel class, which stores it at channel+0xF4.
evidence: slot 10 of vtable 0x0073D2E8 (+0x50) = 0x0054E128, whose assembly is `strb r1,[r0,#0xF4]; bx lr`; identical mask walk to 0x00554CB0; dispatcher opcode 0x20.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat108

evidence: walks the circular list at arg1+8 from *(int**)(arg1+8) and adds `*piVar1` where piVar1 = node-0x14 ints (= -0x50 bytes), i.e. a per-node counter at the head of the -0x58-byte voice/request block; wrapped in the driver monitor at 0x0054D868()+0x1C4; only caller 0x0054DAA4 (the profiler).

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_GetPlaybackInfo
summary: Copies the player's current playback state (a byte at +0x90 plus three 32-bit position/rate words) into the caller's 4-word record under the driver lock. Returns 1 when the player is running, 0 otherwise.
evidence: guarded by player->f_51 ('playing'), copies f_90/f_8C/f_94/f_98, always takes and releases the driver monitor at 0x0054D868()+0x1C4; the same four fields are written by the start path in this batch.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_GetPosition
summary: Returns one of the player's two playback positions (f_78 when `which` is non-zero, f_74 otherwise) under the driver lock, or -1 when the player is not open and 0 when it is open but not playing.
evidence: returns 0xFFFFFFFF when the +0xC open flag or the per-object byte at g_006617E4+self is clear, 0 when +0x51 is clear, else +0x78 / +0x74; the same two fields are the ones 0x0054FE18 uses as start/duration.

name: maybe_Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand(u32 unused, int channel, u32 value, u32 volume, u16 arg5)
summary: Executes one sequence command against a channel: derives the channel's data window from the sequencer (+0x12C), decodes the command's operands with the variable-length reader (0x00662C90), maps volume/pan values (0..127, 1/128 scale) and applies them through the note start/stop helpers.
evidence: bad-instruction decompile around the operand switch, but the 1/128, 0.390625 and 1/127 constants, the 0x3FF mask, calls to 0x0054E260/0x0054E328 (note recycle), 0x00554D60 and 0x00662C90 (the var-len reader) pin it to the sequence interpreter; sequencer pointer is *(int*)(arg2+300).

name: maybe_Sound_Seq_NoteOnThunk
signature: void maybe_Sound_Seq_NoteOnThunk(u32 a, u32 channel, u32 note, u32 velocity, u32 duration, u32 reuse)
summary: Six-argument thunk that forwards straight to Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote (0x0054E88C); it exists so the sequencer can call the note starter through a uniform function-pointer signature.
evidence: single call func_0054E88C(arg2,arg3,arg4,arg5,arg6) with arg1 dropped; no direct caller, i.e. it is stored in a callback table.

name: maybe_Sound_Seq_StepVoiceTrack
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_Seq_StepVoiceTrack(int* cursor, SeqTrack* track, int mode)
summary: Steps one track of a sequence: reads the next opcode from track->f_20 (0xA2/0xA3 are the extended-prefix opcodes), decodes its operands with 0x00662C90 and dispatches to the note/parameter handlers.
evidence: `arg2->f_20 = pbVar12 + 1` is a byte-stream cursor, 0xa2/0xa3 are handled as prefix opcodes, operands decoded by 0x00662C90, and the sequencer pointer *(u32*)(arg2+300) is used for the voice table; no direct caller (reached through the player vtable).

name: Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg
signature: u32 Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg(u32 a, u32* cursor, u32 b, u32 c, u32 kind)
summary: Reads a variable-width operand from a sequence byte stream: kind 1 = u8, 2 = big-endian u16, 3 = 7-bit varint chain (continuation bit 0x80), 4/5 = wider fixed forms. Returns the decoded value and advances the cursor.
evidence: explicit switch with case 3 doing `result = (b & 0x7F) | result << 7` while the 0x80 bit is set - the standard MIDI-style variable-length quantity; case 2 reads two bytes big-endian; g_00662ddc = 0x0000FFFF is the mask constant; called from both sequence interpreters 0x00661974 and 0x00662714.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_SelectFrame
signature: int* maybe_Gfx_Movie_SelectFrame(int* out, int* srcA, int* srcB, int arg4)
summary: Chooses which of two decoded movie surfaces to present: returns an immediate 'same surface' result when both inputs describe the same frame, otherwise compares the frame descriptors, converts the chosen frame's tiles (0x00165CF4) and returns the surface to present.
evidence: `arg2 == arg3 && arg3[10] == 1` short-circuits to result 3; otherwise compares the descriptor words and calls 0x00165CF4 (named Gfx_ConvertTextureTiles by an earlier batch) on the selected surface; g_006b8f20 = 0x007AE5DC is the shared movie state; only caller is maybe_Gfx_Movie_PresentFrame (0x004FD4F4).

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieQueue_Peek
summary: Peeks the next decoded movie frame: under the global movie lock it copies the frame descriptor (surface, two converted addresses, timestamps and flags) at queue->f_28[queue->f_34] into the caller's 11-word record. Returns 1 when a frame is queued.
evidence: g_006b9478 = 0x007CF360 is the global movie monitor; the ring is f_28[head=f_34] with count f_38 and capacity *(int*)(queue+8); 0x0014ECCC/0x0014ECE0 convert the two surface addresses; caller-less, used by the movie player.

name: Gfx_MovieQueue_GetCount
summary: Returns the number of decoded movie frames currently queued, copied out under the global movie lock.
evidence: lock g_006b94b8 = 0x007CF360, `*arg2 = queue->f_38`, unlock, return 1; f_38 is the same count field 0x006B9518/0x006B95E4 modify.

name: Gfx_MovieQueue_Pop
summary: Consumes one decoded movie frame from the ring: advances the head index (wrapping at capacity) and decrements the queued count, under the global movie lock. Returns 0 when the queue is empty.
evidence: `f_34 = (f_34 + 1) % *(int*)(queue+8)` plus `f_38--` inside the g_006b9580 lock, with the empty test on f_38; the exact inverse of 0x006B95E4.

name: Gfx_MovieQueue_Push
summary: Adds a freshly decoded surface to the movie frame ring: converts the surface with 0x00152EA8, records the paired value from 0x0015D4A0, advances the tail index (wrapping at capacity) and increments the count. Returns 0 when the ring is full.
evidence: capacity check `f_38 < *(u32*)(queue+8)`, 0x00152EA8(self, surface, 0) then 0x0015D4A0(self) stored at f_28[tail]/f_2C[tail], tail wrap and f_38++ under the g_006b9690 lock; inverse of 0x006B9518.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_GetReadyFrame
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_Movie_GetReadyFrame(MovieStream* stream, u32 unused, u32* out)
summary: Reports whether a movie stream has a decoded frame ready: resolves the stream's frame source (0x00669A40), checks its state (0x00669708) and returns 0 with the surface in `out`, or 0xE (end of stream / not ready) with a null surface.
evidence: returns literal 0xE for 'no frame', writes f_38 of the frame object into *arg3 when the state byte is 0; 0x00669A40 and 0x00669708 are the frame-source resolve/test pair; 4 callers, all named Gfx_MovieDecoder_* by an earlier batch (0x004FED80, 0x004FEEF4, 0x004FF278, 0x004FF73C).

name: Container_RingBuffer_Push
summary: Pushes one word into a producer/consumer ring: atomically bumps the producer counter, blocks while the ring is full, stores the value at the producer index, publishes the new count and wakes a waiting consumer semaphore.
evidence: exclusive-access loop on ring+0x28 as the producer counter, full test `ring[8] < ring[6]` (count < capacity) waiting on 0x00117D10 (Os_SemaphoreAcquire), index computed by 0x0011CFAC (unsigned modulo), store at *(u32*)(*ring + idx*4), ring[8]++, then 0x00117DC4 (Os_SemaphoreRelease) when ring[9] > 0; callers 0x0056F7A4 and 0x0056FDD0 push object names.

name: maybe_Mem_HeapAllocThrough
signature: void maybe_Mem_HeapAllocThrough(MemHeapHandle* heap, u32 size, u32 flags)
summary: Forwards an allocation to Mem_HeapAlloc (0x0011EDA8) using the heap, the alignment bytes and the type byte cached in the handle at +4/+8/+9/+0xA.
evidence: single call 0x0011EDA8(*(u32*)(arg1+4), size, flags, *(u8*)(arg1+8), *(u8*)(arg1+9), *(char*)(arg1+10)); 0x0011EDA8 is Mem_HeapAlloc per decomp/native_names.json.

name: maybe_Mem_HeapFreeLocked

evidence: *(int*)(arg1+4) is the heap, +0x58 is the lock (the same offset 0x006E7654 locks), 0x0050E5B8 (named maybe_Text_Font_ReleaseRef by an earlier batch) is the per-heap free.

name: maybe_Mem_HeapAllocLocked
signature: u32 maybe_Mem_HeapAllocLocked(MemHeapHandle* handle, u32 size, u32 flags)
summary: Allocates through the heap held in the handle while holding the heap's +0x58 monitor; returns the block address.
evidence: identical argument marshalling to 0x006E75CC (heap at +4, bytes at +8/+9, type at +0xA) but wrapped in the +0x58 monitor and returning the result.

name: maybe_Container_Value_Set
